_readme: ARKANSAS HOLIDAY CALENDAR -- 2026 ONLY, transcribed from a primary state publication.
Every date below appears either on the Arkansas Secretary of State's 2026 State Holidays
sheet or in 5 U.S.C. 6103(a). Nothing here is generated from Ark. Code Ann. 1-5-101(b),
which has still never been read on a primary source -- see the note on the calendar entry.
Adding 2027 means fetching that year's SoS sheet. It 404s today, and until it exists the
engine must keep refusing NOT_PROVISIONED for 2027 rather than deriving the dates.

authority.citation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101 (official state holidays) UNION 5 U.S.C. Sec. 6103 (federal holidays), as required by Ark. R. Civ. P. 6(a)'s "designated as a holiday by the President or Congress of the United States or designated by the laws of this State"
authority.quote: 2026 State Holidays. Legal holidays by authority of Act 304 of 2001 and Amended by Act 561 of 2017.
authority.note: ARKANSAS IS 2026 ONLY, AND THAT CAP IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE CAN EXIST. The seed gate blocked Arkansas because Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101 could not be read on any primary source -- in particular subsection (b), the Saturday-to-preceding-Friday and Sunday-to-succeeding-Monday observance shift. Four secondary publishers agree on that sentence and the gate declined to seed on agreement. THAT IS STILL TRUE: (b) has not been read from primary. What changed on 2026-08-29 is that the dates no longer have to be DERIVED from it. PRIMARY SOURCE FOUND: the Arkansas SECRETARY OF STATE publishes the 2026 sheet at https://www.sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/holidays_2026.pdf (HTTP 200, 204,182 B, 1 page, real text via pypdf), headed verbatim '2026 State Holidays / Legal holidays by authority of Act 304 of 2001 and Amended by Act 561 of 2017.' It CONFIRMS the state list the gate had only from Justia -- including both traps: CHRISTMAS EVE IS PRESENT, and JUNETEENTH AND COLUMBUS DAY ARE ABSENT, which is why the union with the federal list is mandatory and why a state-only calendar would compute EARLY by two days a year. It also SHOWS the Saturday shift operating in the one 2026 instance where it fires: 'July 4 . . . Independence Day (Observed on Friday, July 3, 2026)' -- 4 July 2026 is a Saturday. SO EVERY DATE BELOW IS TRANSCRIBED FROM A PRIMARY STATE PUBLICATION RATHER THAN GENERATED FROM A SHIFT RULE, which is why no unread statute is relied on. NO SUNDAY-LIMB DATE OCCURS IN 2026 -- none of the listed holidays falls on a Sunday -- so the unproven half of (b) never fires here. 2027 AND 2028 ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/holidays_2027.pdf and _2028.pdf both return 404, so those years would have to be derived from the unread subsection and the engine refuses NOT_PROVISIONED on them instead. Same shape as Utah's 2026 cap, and the safe direction. Adding a year means fetching that year's SoS sheet, not extending a rule. THE UNION IS REQUIRED BY THE RULE'S OWN WORDS: ARCP 6(a) defines 'legal holiday' as 'those days designated as a holiday by the President or Congress of the United States OR designated by the laws of this State', so the federal list is co-equal, not a fallback -- the same structure as South Carolina, the platform's first such union. NOT ENCODED, AND BOTH OMISSIONS RUN EARLY: (1) Sec. 1-5-101(a)'s 'an employee's birthday' limb, which is a floating personal-leave day and not a calendar date at all; (2) ARCP 6(a)'s 'other day when the clerk's office is closed', which is per-court and unknowable in advance. See the jurisdiction coverage disclosure for ar in api/_lib/deadline-engine.js.

dates.name: New Year's Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- January 1. Also federal.

dates.name: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.'s Birthday
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- third Monday in January. Also federal.

dates.name: George Washington's Birthday and Daisy Gatson Bates Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- third Monday in February; the combined Arkansas name, printed that way on the SoS sheet. Federally Washington's Birthday.

dates.name: Memorial Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- last Monday in May. Also federal.

dates.name: Juneteenth National Independence Day
dates.derivation: 5 U.S.C. Sec. 6103(a) -- June 19. FEDERAL ONLY: absent from the Arkansas list on the SoS sheet, and reached only through ARCP 6(a)'s union. Omitting it computes EARLY.

dates.name: Independence Day (observed)
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- printed verbatim as 'July 4 . . . Independence Day (Observed on Friday, July 3, 2026)'. 4 July 2026 is a Saturday. This is the ONLY 2026 date where the Sec. 1-5-101(b) shift fires, and it is transcribed from the State's own sheet rather than derived. Federally also observed 2026-07-03 under 5 U.S.C. 6103(b)(1).

dates.name: Labor Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- first Monday in September. Also federal.

dates.name: Columbus Day
dates.derivation: 5 U.S.C. Sec. 6103(a) -- second Monday in October. FEDERAL ONLY: absent from the Arkansas list, reached only through the union. Omitting it computes EARLY.

dates.name: Veterans Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- November 11. Also federal.

dates.name: Thanksgiving Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- fourth Thursday in November. Also federal.

dates.name: Christmas Eve
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- December 24. STATE ONLY: not a federal holiday, and no other jurisdiction in this platform except South Carolina carries 24 December. Omitting it computes EARLY.

dates.name: Christmas Day
dates.derivation: Ark. Code Ann. Sec. 1-5-101(a), as published for 2026 by the Arkansas Secretary of State -- December 25. Also federal.
